_about: What a TLD asks of you, in two kinds. `tlds` is who may register at all:
a name reported AVAILABLE under a restricted TLD should not read as one
you can simply go and buy. `requirements` is what the registry asks of
the name once it is yours — an HTTPS-only zone, a rule about what the
name must be used for. `ds --where` prints both, each with its source.
The two are kept apart because they fail differently. Failing an
eligibility rule means the registry will not sell you the name; failing a
requirement means you can buy it and still not get what you wanted. So a
.app is not restricted — anyone may register one — and listing it as if
it were would be exactly the over-claiming the rest of this file avoids.
Unlike whois.json and pricing.json this file is hand-maintained: no
registry publishes either kind of rule in a machine-readable form, so
there is nothing to generate it from. Every entry therefore carries the
page it was taken from, and that page — not this file — is the authority.
The list covers the TLDs a registrar is likely to offer you; it is not
exhaustive, and a TLD missing from either map is not thereby unencumbered.
Notes say what kind of gate or obligation exists, not the exact legal
test: the wording of a rule changes more often than the fact of one.
Sub-zones inherit, longest suffix first: com.au is looked up as com.au,
then au. Sources last checked 2026-09-02.

eu.note: EU/EEA only: the registrant must be a citizen of, resident in, or an organisation established in the EU/EEA

fr.note: EU presence: the registrant must reside in, or have its registered office in, the EU/EEA or Switzerland

it.note: EU presence: the registrant must be a citizen or resident of, or established in, the EEA, Switzerland, the UK, San Marino or the Vatican

ca.note: Canadian presence: the registrant must meet one of CIRA's Canadian Presence Requirements

au.note: Australian presence: an Australian business or company number, trade mark, or residency is required

us.note: US nexus: the registrant must live in, be organised in, or have a genuine connection to the United States

bd.note: Bangladeshi presence: a citizen with an NID or passport, a business with a trade licence, a registered NGO, a government body, or a foreign entity acting through a local representative

com.bd.note: Bangladeshi presence plus a registered business: a trade licence or certificate of incorporation

net.bd.note: Bangladeshi presence plus a registered business: a trade licence or certificate of incorporation

co.bd.note: Bangladeshi presence plus a registered business: a trade licence or certificate of incorporation

ai.bd.note: Bangladeshi presence plus a registered business: a trade licence or certificate of incorporation

org.bd.note: registered Bangladeshi NGOs, trusts and non-profits only; resale, parking for profit and leasing are prohibited

edu.bd.note: Bangladeshi educational institutions only; resale, parking for profit and leasing are prohibited

sch.bd.note: Bangladeshi schools and educational institutions only

id.bd.note: individual Bangladeshi citizens only, aged 18 or over; resale, parking for profit and leasing are prohibited

gov.bd.note: Bangladeshi government and semi-government bodies only; not sold to the public and not on the registry's price list

mil.bd.note: Bangladeshi armed forces only; not sold to the public and not on the registry's price list

xn--54b7fta0cc.note: Bangladeshi presence, as for .bd; the label must be in Bengali script, and Latin characters are not accepted

br.note: Brazilian presence: a CPF or CNPJ tax registration is required, and a foreign company needs a local representative

gov.note: US government only: federal, state, local and tribal government organisations

mil.note: US Department of Defense only; not sold to the public

edu.note: US institutions accredited by an agency the Department of Education recognises

int.note: intergovernmental organisations established by treaty only

coop.note: cooperatives, and the organisations that serve them, only

bank.note: verified regulated banks only; the registry checks the applicant's charter before delegating
